title: Localization with Hopping Disorder in a Quasiperiodic Synthetic Momentum Lattice
summary: Quasiperiodicity is easily realized with ultracold atoms in optical lattices and has been used to simulate the delocalization-localization transition. Random local potentials can also be implemented by spatial light modulators. Programmable hopping disorder, however, remains difficult to realize in conventional optical lattices. Momentum-space lattice (MSL) offers a platform to address this.
